extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, Medicare payment specialists, policy stakeholders, Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs), and rule commenters (IPPS/LTCH PPS participants)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and criteria for calculating FY 2027 IPPS/LTCH PPS updates, RRC eligibility, Puerto Rico adjustments, and low-volume hospital payment adjustments, including data sources, formulas, and application procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity adjustment definition (section 1886(b)(3)(B)(xi)(II))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(b)(3)(B)(xi)(II) of the Act defines the productivity adjustment as equal to the 10-year moving average of changes in annual economy-wide, private nonfarm business multifactor productivity (as projected by the Secretary for the 10-year period ending with the applicable fiscal year...). The productivity measure referenced is published by BLS as private nonfarm business total factor productivity (TFP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS uses BLS historical TFP data (https://www.bls.gov/productivity/) and IGI's TFP projection methodology (available on CMS website). For this proposed rule, estimate is based on IGI's fourth quarter 2025 forecast; proposed FY 2027 productivity adjustment is 0.8 percent. CMS proposes to use more recent data, if appropriate, to determine the final productivity adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market basket rate-of-increase and interaction with reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicable percentage increase to the operating standardized amount equals the percentage increase in the hospital market basket index, reduced by the productivity adjustment and further reduced as specified for hospitals that do not submit quality data (§412.64(d)(2)) and for hospitals that are not meaningful EHR users (§412.64(d)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS relies on IGI forecasts (Q4 2025 for this proposal) and will update if appropriate with more recent data. See prior rulemakings (e.g., FY 2012, FY 2020) for methodology and implementing regulatory text at 42 CFR 412.64(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable percentage increases by quality submission and EHR meaningful use status (general hospitals)
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2027, proposed updates to hospital-specific rates: 2.4 percent for a hospital that submits quality data and is a meaningful EHR user; 0.0 percent for a hospital that submits quality data and is not a meaningful EHR user; 1.6 percent for a hospital that fails to submit quality data and is a meaningful EHR user; and −0.8 percent for a hospital that fails to submit quality data and is not a meaningful EHR user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These percentages derive from the proposed market basket update (3.2 percent) less the proposed productivity adjustment (0.8 percentage point) and the statutory reductions tied to quality reporting and meaningful EHR use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Puerto Rico hospitals: applicability of market basket adjustments and EHR reduction sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: For subsection (d) Puerto Rico hospitals, the applicable percentage increase will be equal to the rate-of-increase in the hospital market basket for IPPS hospitals in all areas, subject to a reduction of three-quarters of the applicable percentage increase (prior to other statutory adjustments) for Puerto Rico hospitals not considered to be meaningful EHR users under section 1886(b)(3)(B)(ix), and then subject to the productivity adjustment at section 1886(b)(3)(B)(xi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory phase-in: FY 2022 applied three-quarters reduced by 33 1/3 percent; FY 2023 reduction increased to 66 2/3 percent; FY 2024 and subsequent years to 100 percent. For FY 2027 CMS proposes a market basket update of 3.2% less productivity adjustment 0.8% yielding applicable increases of 2.4% (meaningful EHR user) and 0.0% (not meaningful EHR user).

rubrics_metrics.name: RRC bed-size criterion (42 CFR 412.96(b)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the criteria for Rural Referral Center (RRC) qualification is to have 275 or more beds available for use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals meeting this bed-size requirement can qualify as RRCs (subject to other applicable criteria in 42 CFR part 412).

rubrics_metrics.name: RRC alternative pathway: mandatory prerequisites and optional criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A rural hospital with fewer than 275 beds can qualify as an RRC if it meets two mandatory prerequisites (a minimum case-mix index (CMI) and a minimum number of discharges), and at least one of three optional criteria relating to specialty composition of medical staff, source of inpatients, or referral volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 42 CFR 412.96(c)(1)–(5) and FR discussion. CMS refers to the September 30, 1988 Federal Register for additional discussion of optional criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: RRC Case-Mix Index (CMI) prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: A hospital may be classified as an RRC if the hospital's CMI is at least equal to the lower of the median CMI for urban hospitals in its census region (excluding hospitals with approved teaching programs) or the median CMI for all urban hospitals nationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2027 CMS proposes that rural hospitals with fewer than 275 beds must have a FY 2025 CMI of at least 1.7783 (national—all urban) or the regional median CMI (not transfer-adjusted). Proposed CMI values are based on FY 2025 discharges (Oct 1, 2024–Sep 30, 2025) with bills posted through Dec 2025; CMS intends to update values in final rule with additional MedPAR data through March 2026. Hospitals should obtain hospital-specific (not transfer-adjusted) CMI from their MAC; data available via PS&R System; CMI computed on all Medicare patient discharges subject to IPPS MS-DRG payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: RRC discharge prerequisite (national and regional standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify as an RRC, a hospital must have either 5,000 discharges per year (3,000 for an osteopathic hospital) or, if fewer, at least the median number of discharges for urban hospitals in the hospital's census region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2027 CMS proposes to update regional standards based on discharges for urban hospitals' cost reporting periods that began during FY 2024 (Oct 1, 2023–Sep 30, 2024). CMS will update numbers in final rule using latest available cost report data. Because regional medians exceed national standard, 5,000 is the minimum except osteopathic hospitals (3,000).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'best available data' for CMI and discharges (COVID-era adjustment)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS amended regulations to provide for the use of the best available data rather than the latest available data in calculating national and regional CMI and regional discharges criteria (42 CFR 412.96(h)(1) and (i)(1)–(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS uses the individual hospital's CMI value for discharges during the same fiscal year to compute national and regional values; this approach was adopted in light of the COVID-19 PHE and continues to be applied for proposed FY 2027 determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-volume hospital payment adjustment eligibility (temporary definition through Dec 31, 2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: For FYs 2019–2026 and the portion of FY 2027 beginning Oct 1, 2026 and ending Dec 31, 2026, a subsection (d) hospital qualifies as a low-volume hospital if it is more than 15 road miles from another subsection (d) hospital and has less than 3,800 total discharges during the fiscal year (section 1886(d)(12)(C)(i) as amended). 'Road miles' is defined as 'miles' at §412.92(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total discharges means Medicare and non‑Medicare discharges; the hospital's most recently submitted cost report is used to determine total discharges (§412.101(b)(2)(iii)). The extension of temporary changes was implemented via several appropriations and transmittal/change requests (R13564OTN, R13703OTN).

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-volume hospital payment adjustment formula (continuous linear sliding scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary determines the applicable percentage increase using a continuous, linear sliding scale ranging from an additional 25 percent payment adjustment for low-volume hospitals with 500 or fewer discharges to a zero percent additional payment for low-volume hospitals with more than 3,800 discharges in the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory formula specified at §412.101(c)(3)(ii) (see FY 2019 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule). For qualifying hospitals with fewer than 3,800 but more than 500 discharges, the adjustment is calculated by subtracting from 25 percent the proportion of payments associated with discharges in excess of 500 using the formula in §412.101(c)(3)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reversion to pre-ACA low-volume definitions and empirically justifiable adjustment (portion of FY 2027 beginning Jan 1, 2027 onward)
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent further Congressional action, beginning Jan 1, 2027 the low-volume qualifying criteria and payment adjustment revert to statutory requirements prior to FY 2011: to qualify as a low‑volume hospital, a subsection (d) hospital must be more than 25 road miles from another subsection (d) hospital and have less than 200 discharges (to receive a 25% adjustment). The statute also specifies that for discharges in earlier years and for subsequent fiscal years the Secretary must develop an 'empirical relationship'‑based adjustment for hospitals with less than 800 discharges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS previously concluded (FY 2005 analysis) that a 25 percent adjustment for hospitals with less than 200 discharges was most consistent with statutory requirement. Under the reversion, hospitals with 200–799 discharges do not receive an adjustment. CMS uses cost report data to determine total discharges. 'Road miles' definition is at §412.92(c)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and documentation requirements for requesting low-volume hospital adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: A hospital must make a written request for the low-volume payment adjustment to its MAC containing sufficient documentation to establish that it meets the applicable mileage and discharge criteria. The MAC will determine qualification by reviewing submitted data and other available data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the Oct 1, 2026–Dec 31, 2026 portion of FY 2027, a request must be received by MAC no later than Sept 1, 2026 for the adjustment to apply to payments beginning Oct 1, 2026; late requests, if approved, are applied prospectively within 30 days of MAC determination. For the Jan 1, 2027–Sep 30, 2027 portion, a request must be received by MAC no later than Dec 1, 2026 for application beginning Jan 1, 2027; late approved requests applied prospectively within 30 days. A single written request by Sept 1, 2026 may cover both portions. Acceptable documentation can include name and street address of nearest hospital(s), location on a map, distance (use of a web‑based mapping tool is acceptable); MAC may follow up for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources for discharge determination (cost report vs MedPAR)
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2019 and subsequent fiscal years (and earlier FYs 2005–2010), the discharge determination is made based on the hospital's number of total discharges (Medicare and non‑Medicare) using the hospital's most recently submitted cost report. For FYs 2011–2018, MedPAR (Medicare) data were used because only Medicare discharges were considered in those years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS uses cost report data because it includes both Medicare and non‑Medicare discharges and is considered the best available source for total discharges when required by statute/regulation.
